question: What concrete server reply to the handshake (01 01 02) makes the client leave '서버 응답 기다리는중 / WAIT' and advance? Trace where the wait-flag is set on send and cleared on receive, and which response category/op clears it.
independent_finding:
WAIT-FLAG IDENTITY = NET+0x9c (NET = 0x14ad10()+0xa3ac). It is the RENDER-state selector, proven three ways: (1) render dispatcher fo5aee6-5af04: `r2=*(sl+0x6a8)[renderTable]; r3=local(NET); r3+=0x9c; r3=*(r3); lsls#2; r2=table+state*4; r2=*r2; bl 0x1a429c` — indexes renderTable by NET+0x9c. (2) key-handler literal fo5aff2 `ldr r1=0xa448; adds r3,r3,r1` = NET+0x9c absolute. (3) constructor fo5a6de-5a6ec `r2=*(sl+0x6a8); r3=*(sl+0x6b8); str r3,[r2,#0xc]` => renderTable[3]=render-fn 0x72b18; that fn fo72c46 `ldr r3=*(sl+0x9a8)` -> dump_kr fo0xaa880 = '서버 응답 기다리는중'. So NET+0x9c==3 == the WAIT screen.

SET-ON-SEND (handshake): sender fo56a08. fo56a10-56a1a builds NET; fo56a1c-56a1e `movs r0,#3; bl 0x175cdc`; then fo56a22-30 put_u8(1)/put_u8(1)/put_u8(2); fo56a34 flush. State-setter 0x175cdc(mode) fo75d20-75d28: `r2=NET+0x9c; r3=local[-4](=mode arg); str r3,[r2]` => NET+0x9c=mode. It also memsets NET+0xa0..+0x1a0=0 (fo75d16) and NET+0x461=0 (fo75d36). So sending 01 01 02 sets NET+0x9c=3 => shows WAIT. HIGH.

RX FRAME LAYOUT (RX pump fo7e63c): recv into buffer F=r7+8. Wire = [u32 LE total_len][payload]. When F[0](halfword)==0, fo7e6d0 `ldr r3,[r5,#4]; strh r3,[r7,#8]` copies the wire u32 header (at F+4) into F[0]=total_len; F[2]=running cursor; completion test fo7e6de-7e6e2 `cmp cursor,total_len; blt return` => frame ready when received>=total_len (header INCLUDED); then pushed into 4-slot ring at *(sl+0xa38).

RX DISPATCH fo56a40: rx_peek(0x17e9e8)->rx_pop(0x17ea14); F=*P+8; guard fo56a8e `cmp #5; bgt` on F[0]=total_len requires total_len>5 (>=2 payload bytes) else render-only short path; cat=F[8] (fo56abe `ldrb [r3,#8]`), op=F[9] (fo56ad0 `ldrb [r3,#9]`). cat switch fo56ae6-56b48: 0->0x1582e0, 1->0x156bf8, 4->0x156f3c, 5->0x157394, 0x1f->inline0x156bb0, 0x64->0x1581a8.

cat=1 handler fo56bf8, op-switch fo56c46-56c80: op==1->fo56c84 (builds+sends 01 3d <16B acct><...>00; NO state write -> stays WAIT); op==0x3d->fo56d8e (branches on NET+0x38: ==9 sends 04 3e<b>, ==7 sends 1f 00<9B>, else sends 01 3e; each calls 0x175b98(msg,3,1,0)); op==0x3e->fo56e6c.

CLEAR-ON-RECEIVE = cat=1 / op=0x3e ONLY. Handler fo56e6c-56f06: if *(NET+0x1a0)!=0 close old secondary socket via 0x15b390; alloc 0x14-byte node (fo56eba 0x1a42a0(0x14)); fo56ef2 `bl 0x15b10c(node, P, 0xc, -1, 0x99, 9)` opens the secondary game/billing socket, consuming the received frame payload (0x15b10c fo5b176 refs const 0x2710=10000). Then UNCONDITIONALLY (no branch guards it) fo56ef8 `movs r0,#0; bl 0x175cdc` => NET+0x9c=0 (LEAVES WAIT), and fo56f04 `movs r3,#0xd; str [NET+0x38]` => NET+0x38=0xd.

EXHAUSTIVE CLEAR-PATH PROOF: find_callers(0x75cdc)=16 sites. Only two are inside the receive/dispatch region: fo56a1e(arg=3, handshake SET) and fo56efa(arg=0, op=0x3e CLEAR). The other 14 (fo72fca,73f92,73fde,7405e,740aa,741de,74354,74378,7444d2..75006; args mostly 0, one =1) all live in the 0x72xxx-0x75xxx feature-launcher functions (local UI, not server-reply driven). Also 0x175b98 (message-box helper) itself writes NET+0x9c=arg1 (fo75c46-75c50), but every in-scope caller passes mode 3 (op=0x3d: fo56dba/56dfc/56e46) or 7 (cat=0x1f: fo56bce) — never 0. Therefore op=0x3e is the SOLE receive path that clears the WAIT flag.

CONCRETE REPLY: a frame `[u32 LE total_len (>5)][0x01][0x3e][payload]` i.e. cat=0x01, op=0x3e. Minimal WAIT-clear = `06 00 00 00 01 3e` (setState(0) is unconditional). A well-formed server appends the secondary game/billing connection block (~12 bytes read by 0x15b10c) so the follow-on socket connects. Natural login order: server cat1/op1 -> client 01 3d(account) -> server cat1/op3d(sub-negotiation) -> server cat1/op3e(final; clears WAIT).
corrections: The Map claim set is fully CONFIRMED (all 8 claims corroborated by independent disasm). Refinements, not corrections: (a) Claim 4 — the guarded length F[0] is the wire u32 total_len TRUNCATED to a halfword, sourced by the RX pump from the 4-byte header at F+4 via `strh r3,[r7,#8]` (fo7e6d0); guard is total_len>5, consistent with the claim. (b) Claim 5 — op=0x3e's `0x175cdc(0)` (fo56efa) is UNCONDITIONAL: no branch guards it after 0x15b10c returns, so WAIT clears even if the secondary-socket payload is malformed. And op=0x3d 'keeps state 3' is doubly true — its 0x175b98(msg,3,..) actively RE-ASSERTS NET+0x9c=3 (fo75c46-50), it doesn't merely avoid clearing. (c) Claim 8 (truncated in prompt) verified: op=0x3e feeds the frame P to 0x15b10c (size 0xc) to open the secondary socket, refs port/const 0x2710. HONEST UNKNOWN (does not affect WAIT-clearing): the exact byte encoding (IP/port) the op=0x3e payload needs for 0x15b10c to SUCCEED is not fully decoded, and whether a real server jumps straight to op=0x3e vs. sequences op1->op3d->op3e is a black-box question — resolve on device by sending `06 00 00 00 01 3e` and confirming the client leaves WAIT, then sending a longer 01 3e frame carrying the game-server addr and watching for the secondary TCP connect.
